chunks: And it is narrated from Shuʿayb, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
That he was asked about a slave who is freed as a sāʾibah, and he said:
He may take whomever he wishes as his guardian, and upon the one whom he takes as guardian is his liability, and for him is his inheritance.
He said: I said, then if he remains silent until he dies and does not take anyone as a guardian? He said:
His wealth is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.

key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public treasury of the Muslims
key_terms.يَتَوَلَّى: takes someone as patron, guardian, or affiliate in walaʾ

ai.seo_question: What happens to the inheritance of a freed slave who dies without appointing a guardian or walaʾ?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling concerning a freed slave released as sāʾibah, without a fixed walaʾ affiliation. Such a person may choose someone to assume his walaʾ, and that person bears his liability and receives his inheritance. If he dies without assigning anyone, his estate goes to Bayt al-Māl of the Muslims.
